title: The Man Who Flew Around The World On Pudding
sources: Wikipedia / Time / Los Angeles Times — In May 1999, civil engineer David Phillips ('The Pudding Guy') spotted a Healthy Choice mail-in promo offering 500 frequent-flyer miles per 10 UPC barcodes, doubled to 1,000 miles for mail-ins during May 1999.

Snopes / Foodista — Phillips bought 12,150 individual 25-cent chocolate pudding cups at Grocery Outlet stores around Sacramento for about $3,140, donated the pudding to Salvation Army in exchange for help peeling barcodes, and earned 1,253,000 miles plus lifetime AAdvantage Gold status.

lines.text: In nineteen ninety-nine, one guy bought twelve thousand cups of pudding —
lines.caps: In 1999, | one guy | bought | twelve thousand | cups of | pudding —

lines.text: and flew around the world for life.
See, engineer David Phillips spotted twenty-five-cent pudding cups,
stamped with a wild airline promo.
Mail ten barcodes, get five hundred flight miles.
Mail them in May, and the bonus doubled to a thousand.
David pulled out a calculator and grinned.
Ten cups cost two-fifty — meaning flight miles cost pennies.
So he raided ten grocery stores for twelve thousand one hundred fifty cups,
lines.caps: So he | raided ten | grocery stores | for | twelve thousand | one hundred | fifty cups,

lines.text: spending just three thousand one hundred dollars.
He donated every single pudding to charity
so volunteers peeled labels all week.
Soon, one point two five million miles hit his account,
paying for Europe trips plus lifetime VIP status.
Plus an eight-hundred-dollar tax write-off, just for dessert.
